strategy_name: Probability-weighted event evaluation
mechanism: only trade events with publicly announced outcomes, sized by P(event) x payoff vs (1-P(event)) x loss plus time cost
setup_summary: Pre-trade checklist for any announced-outcome event: (1) probability the event occurs, (2) time funds are tied up, (3) upside if something better transpires, (4) downside if the event fails. Take only where probability-weighted gain clearly exceeds weighted loss plus opportunity cost; participate only in publicly-announced events, never rumor.
trigger_invalidation: Abstain/exit when terms change, financing falls through, or the re-estimated probability drops below the required edge.
risk_geometry: Few large positions with wide diversification across mutually-independent events; never one huge bet ('refuse to accept a single, huge bet' - roulette-wheel outlook, p. 79).
quote: To evaluate arbitrage situations you must answer four questions: (1) How likely is it that the promised event will indeed occur? (2) How long will your money be tied up? (3) What chance is there that something still better will transpire—a competing takeover bid, for example? and (4) What will happen if the event does not take place because of anti-trust action, financing glitches, etc.?
chapter_anchor: Part II.B Arbitrage (1988), pp. 66-73
notes: Perps have no announced-price merger spreads; nearest analogs (listings, unlocks, halvings, governance) lack a fixed spread to capture, so direct applicability is LOW. The four-question probability-weighted framework is still the correct pre-trade evaluation template. The 63-year ~20%/yr record with stated fair-test conditions (pp. 72-73) is the book's closest empirical claim.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Margin-of-safety entry threshold
mechanism: only act when price offers substantial expected value over cost; a marginal edge is not worth the exposure
setup_summary: Standing admission rule: an expert emits a CandidateDraft only when expected edge (probability-weighted payoff minus all costs including funding and fees) exceeds a required margin multiple, e.g. EV >= 2x per-unit cost; setups whose edge barely clears cost are skipped. Raises the bar as costs rise.
trigger_invalidation: N/A (standing threshold); a trade that is only 'slightly better than cost' is rejected by construction.
risk_geometry: Entry only at prices giving margin; a geometry whose wider stop / tighter target shrinks margin below the threshold is rejected.
quote: If we calculate the value of a common stock to be only slightly higher than its price, we're not interested in buying. We believe this margin-of-safety principle... to be the cornerstone of investment success.
chapter_anchor: Part II.D 'Value' Investing: A Redundancy (1992), p. 87; cf. Junk Bonds p. 101 ('Margin of Safety' as the three-word secret)
notes: Without an intrinsic-value anchor, margin-of-safety becomes a required edge-over-cost multiple - which binds strongly in perps given funding and taker fees.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Institutional herding and signal crowding
mechanism: organizations mindlessly imitate peers; individually rational actions neutralize collectively, so crowded strategies self-erode and herd behavior creates synchronous exits
setup_summary: Methodology warning: a signal's edge decays as adoption spreads; backtests on already-crowded signals are suspect, and synchronous crowd exits (stops clustered at common levels) amplify drawdowns. V8 should track crowding proxies (OI positioning, funding, perp-vs-spot flow) for its own families and prefer uncrowded triggers.
trigger_invalidation: N/A.
risk_geometry: Extreme crowd alignment is itself a warning (see sentiment_extreme); avoid stop placement at the obvious shared level.
quote: The behavior of peer companies, whether they are expanding, acquiring, setting executive compensation or whatever, will be mindlessly imitated.
chapter_anchor: Part II.F Cigar Butts and the Institutional Imperative (1989), pp. 95-96; toe-stand parable, Part I.C pp. 45-46
notes: Crypto signals crowd within weeks (copy-trading, groupchats, fund flows). The textile toe-stand ('individually rational, collectively irrational' capital spending, p. 46) is the alpha-decay parable for the quant arms race.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Capital-retention value test
mechanism: retained capital must create at least $1 of value per $1 retained or be returned; capital that cannot clear the bar is misallocated
setup_summary: Lifecycle rule: each active expert/parameter variant must demonstrate, on frozen OOS, that deployed capital (per-episode R after funding and fees) returns at least $1 of value per $1 of exposure cost, evaluated on a rolling window; otherwise the variant is deactivated and capital returned to the pool. Mirrors V8's registry gating (PROPOSED -> FORMALIZED -> SCREENING -> REPLICATION -> SHADOW -> PROMOTED).
trigger_invalidation: A variant fails when its OOS per-episode net value is below the cost of the capital it retains, sustained over the rolling window.
risk_geometry: N/A (capital allocation, not entries).
quote: We test the wisdom of retaining earnings by assessing whether retention, over time, delivers shareholders at least $1 of market value for each $1 retained.
chapter_anchor: Part I.A Owner-Related Business Principles #9 (1996), p. 35; cf. Dividend Policy (1984), pp. 124-126
notes: Also warns against 'core-business camouflage' (p. 126): a star family's wins can hide persistent losers elsewhere, so per-family P&L must be evaluated separately - which V8's one-file-per-family layout already enables.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Commodity-market edge structure
mechanism: in a commodity market no participant is much smarter than the dumbest competitor; returns are set by cost structure and patience, not analysis brilliance
setup_summary: Methodology lesson: BTCUSDT perps are the most commoditized market on earth, so price-superiority ('smarter' analysis) is not a durable edge. Edge must come from structure: lower costs (fee/funding discipline, maker execution), asymmetry (sizing, forced-selling exploitation), and patience (not being forced to sell). Falsifiable: experts whose edge claim rests on analysis superiority alone should be gated; structure-based edges prioritized.
trigger_invalidation: N/A.
risk_geometry: Cost discipline: maker/rebate execution, funding-timing; avoid being the counterparty with the highest cost.
quote: In a business selling a commodity-type product, it's impossible to be a lot smarter than your dumbest competitor.
chapter_anchor: Part II.I Preferred Stock (1994), p. 115 (USAir); cf. Part I.C Plant Closings, p. 46 (Burlington $3B capex, stock flat over 20 years)
notes: Corollary of the same essay: capital-reinvestment races in commodity markets neutralize everyone (airline/textile examples) - the quant arms race in crypto means V8's edge must be cost/risk-structural, not informational.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Fixed-fractional risk sizing (1-3% per trade) over Kelly/optimal-f
mechanism: compounding with equalized per-trade risk grows equity fast while capping ruin probability; over-betting (Kelly's 20% stake, optimal-f) produces 77-99% drawdowns and bust
setup_summary: Size every position so the distance to stop represents a fixed small fraction (1-3%) of equity; the book's simulation of a 60%-winning even-money game shows Kelly's 20% stake yields a 77.3% average max drawdown with 2% bust, while 1-2% stakes keep max drawdown under 40% with zero busts. Fixed-fractional risk beat both optimal-f and fixed-ratio in the commodity system (gain-to-pain 7.27 vs 5.70 vs ~2).
trigger_invalidation: Not a strategy trigger; sizing rule. Its validity is bounded by the account-size constraint the book stresses: small accounts cannot risk a small fixed percentage because one contract already exceeds it.
risk_geometry: Position size = (equity x risk%) / stop-distance; compounding uses open+closed equity; stop distance is the 3-SD volatility stop from the stop_distance_atr finding.
quote: There's a reason most money managers use a fixed-risk trading approach. It's because it is a very fast way to build equity, and risk is equalized on every position by the sizing.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 11, Sizing Summary
notes: With perp leverage 20-100x, position sizing is where over-leverage does its damage; the book's simulation (Kelly = 20% stake, 77% drawdown, 2% bust) is the strongest available argument for V8's RiskGate heat cap and per-trade risk limits. Also a methodological warning: optimal-f ignores open-equity giveback and concurrent-trade overlap, so its TWR math is unusable for a system with open positions - V8's heat cap should be equity-fraction based, not TWR-based.
book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

strategy_name: Diversification across uncorrelated groups; cap same-group exposure
mechanism: instruments within a group move in tandem, so concentrated group exposure multiplies drawdown; spreading across uncorrelated groups keeps profit roughly constant while cutting drawdown ~20-25%
setup_summary: Trade instruments from different groups rather than several members of one group; 'first-N-in-a-group': take the first N signals from each group and cap group count. The book's 8-commodity test: all-currencies vs diversified portfolios made near-identical profit ($528,888 vs $517,983) but the diversified set had ~25% lower average and ~20% lower max start-trade drawdown.
trigger_invalidation: Risk-portfolio rule, not a market trigger; it caps how many correlated exposures may coexist.
risk_geometry: Portfolio-level: max simultaneous exposures per correlated group = N; apply start-trade drawdown as the small-account survival metric.
quote: These results illustrate the diversification advantage. The average max draw-down is about 25 percent lower in the diversified set, and the maximum draw-down is about 20 percent less than the non-diversified portfolios', but the total profit is about the same.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 12, Diversification (beginning of Part 1)
notes: For single-instrument BTCUSDT the cap is trivial; it becomes load-bearing if V8 expands to ETH/alt perps, where the entire crypto market is effectively ONE correlated group - BTC, ETH and majors would count as same-group exposures (beta ~0.8+), so naive multi-coin 'diversification' would not reduce drawdown the way this book's diversified commodity basket did. Funding-basis and BTC-dominance structure are the crypto-specific group dimensions.
book: Building Reliable Trading Systems - Tradable Strategies That Perform As They Backtest and Meet Your Risk-Reward Goals 2013

strategy_name: Hidden composition deterioration (decompose aggregates; forced flow masks quality)
mechanism: Headline aggregates stay statistically static while the composition inside them shifts toward lower quality (rising share of interest-only/negative-amortizing instruments, rising share of forced flow disguised as voluntary), so deterioration is invisible until it is terminal.
setup_summary: Measurement discipline for feature engineering: do not read aggregate flow/OI/participation stats at face value; decompose into forced vs voluntary components. In perps the 'involuntary prepayment' analog is liquidation/forced-close volume as a share of total volume and OI split by leverage bucket; Burry's static-FICO/rising-IO-ARM analog is static aggregate credit metrics with a rising high-risk instrument share. Vinny proved the method: sifting pool data revealed 'stunningly high delinquency rates' and no real earnings.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: rising forced-flow share or high-risk composition share while headline volume/OI is flat. Invalidated if the decomposition reverts, or if the predicted default/liquidation surge does not follow within the observation window.
risk_geometry: Not a trade; an evidence discipline for feature-group construction (which ratios enter marketstate).
quote: 'Involuntary prepayment' sounds better than 'default.'
chapter_anchor: Chapter 1, 'A Secret Origin Story' (Vincent Daniel's pool analysis)
notes: Directly implementable: perp venues publish liquidation volumes and OI breakdowns. The lesson generalizes Burry's observation that 'these measures could stay roughly static, but the overall pool ... was worsening in quality.'
book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

strategy_name: Defined-downside tail protection with counterparty survival and MTM collateral
mechanism: A tail bet with capped premium and many-x upside only pays off if the party you bought protection from survives the very event you are insured against; demanding mark-to-market collateral posting on the contract preserves the payoff.
setup_summary: Burry's CDS construction lesson: when tail risk is structurally mispriced (buyers paying 250bp for protection on the worst triple-B pools while a triple-A seller charges 12bp on the same bonds re-rated through a synthetic CDO), place the defined-loss bet before the market reprices it, then wait through mark-to-market pain. Two execution constraints: (1) buy protection only from counterparties that will survive the insured event — Burry never bothered calling Bear or Lehman because they were most exposed; (2) demand MTM collateral posting so the hedge's value is not destroyed by counterparty failure. 'I'm not making a bet against a bond. I'm making a bet against a system.'
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: structural mispricing of tail risk (wide gap between what sellers charge and what odds imply). Invalidated if the mispricing reprices before the position is fully on, or if the counterparty cannot post collateral / is itself at risk from the event.
risk_geometry: Entry: premium stream (book: ~2.5%/yr on triple-B for up to ~6 years of an expected 30-year loan). Stop: none; loss capped at the premium stream. Target: many multiples of premium on the event (odds felt like 2:1, offered at 6:1 to 10:1). Collateral/MTM posting on the contract is mandatory.
quote: There was no point buying insurance from a bank that went out of business the minute the insurance became valuable.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2, 'In the Land of the Blind' (Burry's first CDS trades, May 2005)
notes: The CDS instrument itself does not exist in perps (no options/insurance tape), so the trade construction is DEFER_GATED. The transferable risk rules are venue-level: cap single-venue exposure, model exchange/liquidation-engine failure in the simulator, and treat any hedge's counterparty survival as part of the hedge's value. Direction of the underlying trade was SHORT, but the extracted rule is direction-neutral.
book: The Big Short - Inside the Doomsday Machine 2011

strategy_name: Preset-time no-movement exit (time-stop)
mechanism: a position that produces no favorable price movement or no market-condition change within a preset time window is a dead thesis; exit before the price stop is hit
setup_summary: For every new position define a preset movement deadline (half-cycle of the momentum oscillator ~= 8 bars, scaled by dividing the max holding period by ~8-9 to choose the trading timeframe). If the position makes no significant favorable price movement, or (for exhaustion entries) the market condition does not change in the trade's direction, by the deadline - exit regardless of stop distance. Re-establishing the position later is always permitted.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: deadline elapses without significant favorable movement / without condition change. Known cost: sometimes you exit and the market then moves in your original direction; the rule is accepted to improve overall performance.
risk_geometry: Time-based exit independent of the price stop; stop remains as backstop; timeframe chosen so that holding period = 8-9 bars (e.g. 45-minute holding -> 5-minute bars).
quote: New positions must make some price movement in your favor within a preset amount of time. Should you not get any significant price movement within that time limit, exit.
chapter_anchor: Ch6 (pp. 302-307) 'Using Time as Part of Your Risk Management', 'The Hardest Part of Any Strategy Is the Exit'
notes: Directly implementable as a V8 lifecycle/dead-thesis rule: dead-thesis is already distinguished from stop exits in V8, and this adds a third exit - time-invalidation. Deterministic and cheap; no wall clock needed (bar-count based). Corroborates the time_stop starter slug.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Minimum 4:1 reward-to-risk admission rule
mechanism: only take trades with measured technical reward-to-risk >= 4:1, computed with a smaller-timeframe stop and a larger-timeframe target; fixed R-multiple exits are rejected in favor of expectation/time management
setup_summary: Before entry, measure R:R from the chart: identify an Area of Opportunity in the larger timeframe, then use a smaller timeframe to locate a defined-risk setup - stop level from the smaller-timeframe setup, target from the larger timeframe. Do not take any trade below 4:1; if none exists on the timeframe, drop down a timeframe or two until a 4:1 opportunity appears. Do not manage trades to a fixed 3:1 target ('myth'): winning trades are managed by expectation, time, and market condition.
trigger_invalidation: Admission gate, not a trigger: any candidate with R:R < 4:1 is rejected at admission (or moved to a lower timeframe where 4:1 exists).
risk_geometry: Mixed-timeframe R computation (small-TF stop, large-TF target); R:R >= 4:1 required at admission; management is dynamic (time/condition based), not fixed-R.
quote: Measure the technical reward to risk from the charts and do not take any trades that are less than 4:1 reward-to-risk ratio (R:R).
chapter_anchor: Ch5 (pp. 275, 280-281) 'Reward-to-Risk Considerations' & 'Conclusion: Trading Rules'; Ch6 (p. 305) 'The 3:1 Risk/Reward Myth'
notes: Candidate RiskGate admission rule (V8's RiskGate currently uses target_r/stop_r fixed geometry). Note the 4:1 gate targets pre-transition balance-area setups with phase-transition upside; a fixed minimum-R gate interacts with V8's 1.0R targets and would need registry evaluation. Also the book's rejection of fixed 3:1 management argues for keeping V8's dynamic exits.
book: New Frontiers in Technical Analysis - Effective Tools and Strategies for Trading and Investing 2011

strategy_name: Stop placement away from round-number levels
mechanism: Round-number and quarter-fraction price levels concentrate resting orders and act as intraday support/resistance; stops placed exactly at them are preferentially run, so offset stops from these levels.
setup_summary: Do not place buy stops exactly on round levels (bond/note fractions 08/32, 16/32, 24/32; grains 0.5/1.0; meats 0.25/0.50/0.75); place buy stops above and sell stops below those levels because they act as intraday support/resistance and collect stop orders. Crypto analogue: avoid stops exactly at psychological round prices (e.g., 100,000).
trigger_invalidation: N/A - a stop-placement risk rule, not a trade thesis.
risk_geometry: Stop price offset by a small buffer from the round level; applies to both entry stops and protective stops.
quote: You generally want to put your buy stops above these levels and your sell stops below those levels as those prices can act as support and resistance on an intraday basis.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 12, 'Other Tactics and Techniques' (p.214)
notes: Well-corroborated across the library (stop-run/stop-hunt literature). Crypto perps show strong clustering at round figures; no gaps makes fills at these levels more likely to be stopped exactly, and high leverage magnifies the cost of being run. Implementation: RiskGate offset for stops near integer/round price deciles.
book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

strategy_name: Fractional risk-capital sizing (50% margin, 20% per-trade risk)
mechanism: Capping deployed margin and per-trade risk to fractions of equity preserves the account through losing streaks; risking the full account on one position is ruin-concentrated.
setup_summary: Trade only risk capital (money you can afford to lose). Use at most ~50% of investment capital as margin for any one trade, and risk at most ~20% of initial capital on a single trade; do not deploy 100% of margin capacity into one position, which a small adverse move can wipe out. Position size is a function of stop distance and the risk budget.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - a sizing rule; violated if per-trade risk exceeds the fixed equity fraction.
risk_geometry: Position size = per-trade risk budget / stop distance; account-level margin cap (50%) and per-trade risk cap (20%).
quote: Some money managers suggest using only 50 percent of your investment capital in any one trade and then risking 20 percent of your initial capital in that trade.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 11, 'A Dose of Reality' (p.196)
notes: Directly feeds RiskGate deterministic admission: per-trade risk cap and heat cap on notional exposure. With perp leverage (10-125x), the 20% per-trade risk cap becomes even more binding. Book also stresses never risking the whole account ('It's okay to lose your shirt, just don't lose your pants...').
book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

strategy_name: Proportional time stop - half-and-half thesis check
mechanism: A position's value decays with time if the thesis does not pay; re-evaluating at the halfway point of the expected horizon (or when half the premium/time value is gone) prevents holding a wasting position to full expiry.
setup_summary: Enter with an explicit expected time horizon for the thesis to pay (e.g., 6 months for the coffee call). At the halfway point of that horizon - or when half the time/premium value has eroded - re-evaluate: exit, trim/salvage, or re-commit; do not silently hold a position whose time thesis has decayed.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - a time-management rule; triggers re-evaluation, not a hard exit by itself.
risk_geometry: Expiry set at half the expected horizon (proportional time stop); exit/trim if no confirmation by then.
quote: If half of the time value or half of the premium value erodes, reevaluate the position. Either get out of the options or salvage some premium by liquidating a portion of your position.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 13, 'Options Trading Steps' (p.224)
notes: Framed for options time decay, but the general rule - check the thesis at a fixed fraction of the expected horizon - transfers to perps and refines V8's expiry_bars: expiry becomes a proportional-thesis check (e.g., by expiry/2 the trade must be within X of target) instead of a fixed bar count. Corroborates the 'time stop' starter concept.
book: A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics - How to Profit Using Pivot Points, Candlesticks & Other Indicators 2004

strategy_name: Hold to compound; churn pays a transfer tax every cycle
mechanism: Realizing gains periodically pays a tax/transfer cost on each cycle; a single internally-compounding holding beats a sequence of equal-return round-trips by a huge factor (book's $1 doubling example: ~$25,250 vs ~$692,000 over 20 years). Every asset switch incurs a 'transfer tax'.
setup_summary: For the V8 simulator: quantify the compounding drag of turnover the way the book quantifies tax drag — taker fees, funding, and slippage paid on each round-trip compound against a family's gross edge. Falsifiable: simulate two variants of the same family at identical gross per-trade edge but different turnover and show net results diverge by the cost compound, matching the book's arithmetic.
trigger_invalidation: Methodology check, not a trade: a high-turnover expert family must beat the low-turnover variant on net OOS after costs, or its gross advantage is a measurement artifact.
risk_geometry: N/A - cost-model lesson for src/v8/simulator.py (fill-at-close, Binance USDM cost model, funding accrual).
quote: this deferred tax liability is equivalent to a very large transfer tax that is payable only if we elect to move from one asset to another.
chapter_anchor: Part V.G Deferred Taxes, pp.195-196; Part V.J Taxation and Investment Philosophy, pp.205-206 (Li'l Abner tale)
notes: Perps have no capital-gains tax, but funding + taker fees + slippage are the perp 'transfer taxes' paid on every position switch, and they compound identically. The 27:1 arithmetic is exact and reproducible, hence DESIGN_INFERENCE rather than NARRATIVE.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Owner earnings: net of maintenance costs, not 'cash flow'
mechanism: Sustainable economic earnings = reported + non-cash charges - required maintenance reinvestment; quoting 'cash flow' (a)+(b) without subtracting maintenance (c) overstates sustainability, because 'over a five- or ten-year period, they must make the investment - or the business decays'.
setup_summary: For V8 backtest economics: compute net edge = gross PnL - mandatory costs to stay in the market (funding paid while holding, rollover, borrow). A family that looks profitable on gross PnL may be net-negative once these maintenance costs are netted, mirroring the (a)+(b)-(c) formula. Falsifiable: re-rank expert families on net-after-maintenance edge and compare registry decisions.
trigger_invalidation: Methodology check: any family whose edge depends on omitting persistent maintenance costs (funding on a 24/7 market) is rejected or re-evaluated on the net basis.
risk_geometry: N/A - evaluation/attribution lesson; funding accrual belongs in the simulator cost model and lifecycle hold accounting.
quote: the company or investor believing that the debt-servicing ability or the equity valuation of an enterprise can be measured by totalling (a) and (b) while ignoring (c) is headed for certain trouble.
chapter_anchor: Part V.D Owner Earnings and the Cash Flow Fallacy, pp.185-186 (Scott Fetzer example)
notes: Funding is the perp maintenance cost par excellence: a long held through positive funding pays it continuously. The book's warning that EBITDA-style presentation is used to 'justify the unjustifiable' parallels promotional backtest reporting that omits funding and fees.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Beware the horse that walks fine (seller-timed quality)
mechanism: The counterparty/seller knows more than the buyer and times the transaction for when the asset 'walks just fine'; buying into the most flattering presentation of quality is inherently adversely selected.
setup_summary: A psychological guardrail for V8: when a setup's public justification is at its most consensus-flattering (peak open interest into highs, euphoric narrative), treat entry as adversely selected against the crowd and require independent verification instead of seller/crowd-supplied optimism. Falsifiable as a filter: reject candidates whose triggering narrative is consensus-positive at the moment of entry.
trigger_invalidation: Filter, not a trade: candidates admitted on the strength of apparent quality at the point of maximum flattery are rejected; the filter is validated by comparing OOS results with the filter on vs off.
risk_geometry: N/A - psychology/filter lesson; pairs with the failed-breakout and liquidity_sweep families' reliance on frozen refs rather than narrative.
quote: the seller of a business practically always knows far more about it than the buyer and also picks the time of sale - a time when the business is likely to be walking 'just fine.'
chapter_anchor: Part IV.D Sound Acquisition Policies, p.151; also On Selling One's Business (financial-maneuverer buyer type, pp.155-156)
notes: In perps the 'seller' is the retail crowd and liquidity providers; the book's warning that apparent quality at sale-time masks adverse selection maps to buying momentum at the point where everyone already knows the story. Also relevant: the ailing-horse anecdote ('when he's walking fine, sell him').
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Only swing at pitches in the happy zone
mechanism: Disciplined selectivity: a hitter who swings at everything outside his zone drops from a .344 hitter to a .250 hitter; infrequency of acceptable opportunities is a sign of discipline, not of failure.
setup_summary: For V8 expert screening: enforce a quality bar so a family only emits candidates meeting a minimum evidence threshold; the rarity of qualified candidates is expected ('infrequency of business acquisition may safely be predicted'). Falsifiable: a family forced to trade all near-threshold setups underperforms the same family trading only above-threshold setups on frozen OOS.
trigger_invalidation: Methodology check: any family whose edge vanishes when the quality bar is tightened is evidence that the bar, not the setup, was the source of apparent edge.
risk_geometry: N/A - selection policy for the lab runner and registry screening gates.
quote: If I have to bite at stuff that is out of my happy zone, I'm not a .344 hitter. I might only be a .250 hitter.
chapter_anchor: Epilogue, pp.208 (Ted Williams quote); also infrequency-of-acquisitions passage, p.151
notes: Perp markets present near-infinite 'pitches' 24/7, so the selectivity lesson is directly testable: does the V8 family emit candidates selectively or does it trade every setup? The book frames patience as productive (dealing 'from strength').
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: The fat wallet is the enemy of superior results (capacity decay)
mechanism: Capacity limits and base effects: high growth rates self-destruct as the base balloons ('in a finite world, high growth rates must self-destruct'), and a minimum-deployable size shrinks the opportunity universe.
setup_summary: For V8: every candidate edge must be evaluated at a realistic deployment size, because perp depth and slippage scale with notional; a family that looks good at small notional may show decaying per-unit edge as size grows. Falsifiable: simulate each family at increasing notional and show net edge per unit declines beyond a capacity threshold.
trigger_invalidation: Methodology check: registry promotion requires the frozen-OOS net edge to survive at the deployment-size simulation, not just at minimal notional.
risk_geometry: N/A - capacity/slippage lesson for src/v8/simulator.py and lab sizing.
quote: A fat wallet ... is the enemy of superior investment results.
chapter_anchor: Epilogue, pp.207-208 (Sagan bacteria passage; $100M minimum-deployable rule)
notes: The book's '$100 million minimum' shrinks the universe; the perp analog is that the exploitable depth of BTCUSDT at a given time window bounds how much of a backtest edge is real. Base effects (Sagan's bacteria) warn against extrapolating early-family results.
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Double-dip decomposition: fundamental gain + one-time re-rating
mechanism: Past returns came from two components: gains in intrinsic value plus a one-time bonus from market 'correction' of valuations; the re-rating component is not repeatable, so future returns have a single-dip.
setup_summary: For V8 attribution: decompose each family's realized PnL into underlying-move capture vs. microstructure/funding timing vs. level-correction effects. A family whose edge is mostly a one-time 'correction' of a stale level (e.g., a mean-reversion to an anchor that has itself repriced) must not be extrapolated. Falsifiable: split OOS PnL by source; a family whose edge is dominated by non-repeatable correction components is not registry-promotable.
trigger_invalidation: Evaluation frame, not a trade: verdicts on a family must be based on the repeatable component of its PnL, not the total.
risk_geometry: N/A - attribution lesson; supports the lab's per-episode logging and frozen-OOS verdict discipline.
quote: our performance to date has benefited from a double-dip: (1) the exceptional gains in intrinsic value that our portfolio companies have achieved; (2) the additional bonus we realized as the market appropriately 'corrected' the prices of these companies.
chapter_anchor: Epilogue, pp.207-208
notes: For perps, the decomposition is directional-move capture vs. funding accrual vs. liquidation-timing; funding-heavy profits are the analog of the one-time re-rating bonus and should not be extrapolated as an independent edge (funding is a transfer, not a source).
book: The Essays of Warren Buffett - Lessons for Corporate America 1998

strategy_name: Evaluate on look-through drivers, not the short-term scoreboard
mechanism: Performance should be judged by the economic driver (business value) rather than by short-term market price; the scoreboard (price) is the final arbiter in the long run, but decisions are made by watching the playing field.
setup_summary: For V8: an expert should be evaluated on whether its causal behavior/mechanism actually occurred and its MarketState inputs were valid, not on short-window PnL; price outcome is the final arbiter at OOS time, but evidence gates and registry decisions are mechanism-based. Falsifiable: an episode is scored on mechanism validity (setup conditions, still_valid holds) before PnL is examined.
trigger_invalidation: Evaluation frame: verdicts that flip purely with short-window PnL noise are rejected in favor of mechanism-based scoring.

strategy_name: Scale-out and stop-management rules (half-off at 100% margin return, trailing stops, close-only stops)
mechanism: locking in half the position at a target and trailing the stop on the remainder converts a winner's R:R asymmetry into guaranteed partial profit while preserving upside; close-only stops filter intraday noise so a correct thesis is not stopped out
setup_summary: Exit/risk rules extracted from the book: (1) if a trade makes 100% of the initial margin requirement, liquidate half the position (single contract: take the whole trade off) and trail the stop on the remainder above/below the 3-day and 9-day moving averages; (2) do NOT move a stop to breakeven while price is still at breakeven - wait until price has actually advanced, or you get stopped out prematurely on a correct thesis; (3) use close-only stops when a thesis depends on the close ('a regular stop could be triggered on an intraday move, and then the market could snap right back up and take me out of the trade'); (4) always use stops and know the loss objective before entry; (5) risk/reward plan from entry ('a trading plan should include the initial entry position, the risk management loss objective, and the targeted profit objective').
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches the scale-out target (100% margin return) -> reduce half, trail stop. Never trigger: moving a stop to breakeven prematurely; holding without a stop.
risk_geometry: exit-first design: stop = close-only beyond structure (below low / above high); target = opposite pivot or MA level; expiry = bars; scale-out = 1/2 at first target, remainder trailed.
quote: Rule of thumb: If you make 100 percent of your initial margin requirement, get out of the trade if you are a one-contract trader. Multiple position traders should move stops down and get out of half of their positions.

strategy_name: Ruin Avoidance - Anything Times Zero Is Zero
mechanism: one event that zeros the account destroys the entire compounded record no matter how good every other year was; leverage is the typical cause because a single margin-call day converts an open position into forced liquidation
setup_summary: Design the book so no single event can wipe it out: 'anything times zero is zero... if there is just one year with a zero, it's all over'; 'throughout history, it is leverage that wipes people out'; 'there only has to be one day you cannot meet a margin call.' Buffett cites LTCM (25x net worth), Gen Re post-9/11 (collateral calls on shrunken capital), and GEICO's $94M loss on $72K of premium as the failure mode. For V8: leverage is capped so a worst-case gap/cascade/liquidation move cannot breach the wipeout boundary; 'you cannot farm-out risk management.'
trigger_invalidation: Standing constraint; it binds only when sizing and leverage decisions are being made, and it is the reason Buffett accepts lower returns ('Why expose the company to ruin and disgrace for an extra percentage point of return?').
risk_geometry: Position size and leverage capped so a maximum-adverse-excursion scenario cannot force liquidation; keep a reserve so a forced-seller moment finds you with dry powder, not under margin.

strategy_name: Opportunity-Cost Selection (every trade competes with the best alternative; omission is the biggest cost)
mechanism: each commitment is justified only if it beats the best available alternative; mediocre opportunities are costly because they consume the capacity to act on great ones, and the largest cost is failing to act on an understood high-conviction idea ('thumb-sucking')
setup_summary: 'Life is a whole series of opportunity costs' - 'to measure opportunity cost, take your best available opportunity versus all other options.' In trading, with one exposure per direction, every candidate episode competes and only the best fills the slot; a filled slot must beat the next-best idea (rank by expected value). Symmetrically, errors of omission dominate: Buffett stopping Wal-Mart at $23 cost shareholders $10B; Munger's Belrich Oil refusal cost $200M. Not acting on a high-conviction understood setup is the most expensive mistake.
trigger_invalidation: Standing selection discipline; it binds at every admission decision and every capacity allocation.
risk_geometry: Capacity discipline is the mechanism: one active exposure per direction makes the next-best idea the explicit opportunity cost of filling the slot.

strategy_name: What vs. When - No Macro Timing
mechanism: predicting which side of an edge wins (the 'what') is tractable; predicting the timing of market swings (the 'when') is not - 'we're predicting how people will swim against the current. We're not predicting the current itself.'
setup_summary: Buffett and Munger refuse market-timing and macro forecasts ('you can't dance in and out of businesses based on forecasts'), keep cash as a default option when nothing is cheap, and concentrate on individual opportunities. 'To think about what will happen versus when is a far more efficient way to behave.' For V8: regime filters and macro-timing components should stay absent by default; edge hypotheses are conditional on observable microstructure, not on forecasts of the direction or timing of the market.
trigger_invalidation: Standing design constraint - it excludes an entire class of components (market-timing and regime-forecast models) rather than defining an episodic trigger.
risk_geometry: Cash is the default option when no asymmetric setup exists; there is no obligation to hold a position in every regime.

strategy_name: Probe-and-confirm pyramiding (position scaling on confirmation)
mechanism: build a pre-planned position in tranches, adding size only after price confirms the thesis by moving in the intended direction
setup_summary: Before the first trade, fix the total intended position size. Enter 20% as a probe; add the next 20% only if price moves in the intended direction (proof the judgment is correct), another 20% at a further-extended confirming level, then after a normal countertrend correction holds at the prior add level take the final 40%. If the probe moves against you, close it or wait; never sustain a loss above 10% on the position.
trigger_invalidation: An adverse move after any tranche invalidates the confirmation: no further adds until the price again confirms; the probe itself is cut or frozen rather than averaged down.
risk_geometry: Entry: staged tranches (20/20/20/40%) at successively confirming prices (higher for longs, lower for shorts); stop: 10% against original purchase price; target: ride the swing, no fixed R-multiple; expiry: none stated, position held while trend holds.
quote: The first probe or transaction is crucial; it is the key to this technique. After the first transaction, do not make a second until you have confirmed that your judgment is correct.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 4 'The Crash of 1907' (pp. 64-65)
notes: The inverse rule is stated in Ch. 5 (Cotton King): Livermore's $2.7M loss came from dollar-averaging DOWN into losing cotton instead of cutting it - i.e., adds are only permitted on confirmation, never against the thesis. strategy_name: 10% per-position hard stop
mechanism: a fixed percentage of the original purchase price is the maximum tolerable loss per position, enforced mechanically regardless of the position's story
setup_summary: Any long or short position is closed if it loses more than 10% against the original purchase price, unconditionally - even if the underlying judgment later proves right. Livermore framed this as his lifelong bucket-shop inheritance: all he ever wanted to lose in any one stock is ten percent.
trigger_invalidation: The cap is unconditional; the rule itself has no invalidation. Livermore's catastrophic losses (e.g., holding losing cotton) came precisely from breaking this rule.
risk_geometry: Entry: any; stop: fixed 10% of original purchase price (not ATR-scaled, not swing-point); target/expiry: not specified by this rule.

strategy_name: Model-conviction doubling (adding size to a losing position)
mechanism: Conviction in the model converts a losing trade into a signal to add size ('merely redoubled the bet'); at leverage this turns a paper loss into a potentially catastrophic loss, and when traders are their own watchdogs there is no independent brake.
setup_summary: RiskGate rule: prohibit or strictly cap scaling into a position that is moving against the entry thesis purely because model conviction is unchanged; any size addition must be justified by a new, independently observable condition, not by conviction. Canonical case: Hilibrand lost $400M on a Salomon mortgage bet and coolly proposed doubling the commitment; management refused the doubling and the position eventually recovered, but the pattern is the risk.
trigger_invalidation: n/a - the rule holds regardless of thesis; conviction is not a valid re-entry signal.
risk_geometry: Fixed per-episode size; no pyramiding into losers; admission must flow through a deterministic RiskGate because 'the traders were their own watchdogs' is the failure mode - LTCM had no Gutfreund-type brake and no independent risk manager, and risk approvals went to Hilibrand/Haghani 'who would fight relentlessly for what they wanted.'

strategy_name: Rule-of-thumb regime flip (market acceptance thresholds are mutable)
mechanism: A single celebrated success can suspend a long-standing market acceptance rule, repricing the whole asset class on a new criterion while the prior regime's incumbents decay.
setup_summary: Equity-IPO market: pre-1995 rule of thumb required four consecutive profitable quarters before selling a tech company to the public; Netscape's loss-making August 1995 IPO established 'rapid growth, not profits' as the new acceptance criterion. Incumbent SGI, peaking at $44 the week after the offering, fell steadily to $8 over the following four years and its CEO was fired. Lesson for V8: the market's acceptance/valuation threshold is itself a regime variable, not a constant - a static 'still_valid' rule tied to a stale threshold can break.
trigger_invalidation: Invalidated if a market that suspends an acceptance rule fails to reprice incumbents (i.e., if no repricing follows the threshold flip).
risk_geometry: None stated (equity-IPO structure, not a trade).

strategy_name: Edge decay and forced self-cannibalization
mechanism: A working edge is systematically self-limiting: the constituency earning from the current product resists the change that would replace it, while the underlying force (Moore's law) commoditizes the edge from below - so the incumbent that defends the present over the future loses.
setup_summary: Clark's explicit rule: a technology company 'needed always to be looking to destroy itself. If it didn't, someone else would.' SGI refused to build the sub-$5,000 low-end machine that would cannibalize its high-margin workstations and was displaced by the PC/Microsoft. Direct V8 lesson: a currently-profitable strategy variant's constituency resists replacement, so challenger evaluation must be institutionalized and forced (V8's frozen-OOS challenger + registry protocol does this); the currently-best variant is the most likely to be over-trusted.
trigger_invalidation: Invalidated if incumbents that defend the current product systematically outperform self-cannibalizers over horizons the thesis cares about.

strategy_name: Premature entry as failure mode (correct thesis, wrong timing)

setup_summary: Clark's telecomputer thesis was directionally correct (interactive home computing) but entered years early at unbuildable cost: 'too expensive to build' and 25M Internet users later, the same idea grafted onto the Internet succeeded. Trading analogue: a setup with correct direction but entered before the confirmation/cost-feasibility condition is met still loses; entry timing and build-cost constraints are as binding as thesis validity.
